description: Add field placements to an EXISTING prepared free-signature document and send it to its participants. This tool does not upload, prepare, or itself sign a document. Use only when sending is requested and preparation is confirmed; for a pending preparation, check status first. Reuse the matching documentId and fileId from preparation. All coordinate arrays apply to that single PDF and must refer to its existing participants. The server downloads the current PDF to read page dimensions for conversion; it does not discover intended field locations or retrieve participants. Obtain the participants and intended placements before calling. This tool uses only the prepared document's fileId, not documentBase64, documentUrl, storageFileId, uploadId, or chatgptFile. Maximum downloaded PDF size: 26214400 bytes. To start a new document from any of the five file sources, use a preparation tool instead. Set coordinateSystem to page_percent. ALL field types use the same page-relative percentages: (0,0) is the top-left of the visible page, x increases rightward, y increases downward; 100 is the full page width or height, not 1. pageNumber is zero-based (0 is the first page). x/width are percentages of page width; y/height are percentages of page height. Positions must be >= 0, sizes > 0, x + width <= 100 and y + height <= 100. Example: x=10,y=80,width=30,height=10 starts 10% from the left and 80% from the top, covering 30% of page width and 10% of its height. The server reads each PDF page and handles backend units and field-specific conversions. Do not supply pixels, PDF points, or backend coordinates, or guess a placement from an unrelated image. Use the actual visible page and the user's intended field location. Unrepresentable placements, unreadable PDFs, 180-degree rotated placement pages, and text fields on rotated/cropped pages are rejected before sending; provide a flattened PDF if requested by the error. Provide at least one signatureCoordinates entry; optional coordinate arrays default to empty. Every coordinate's signatoryEmail must identify a participant in this document. Role values and behavior: signer signs the contract; reviewer is a view-only participant who can see the contract but has no action to perform; approver reviews and approves the contract without signing. Map a requested viewer to reviewer, and a requested reviewer who must approve to approver. The literal value viewer is not accepted. If the intended action is unclear, ask before choosing a role. Returns sent when rollout succeeds, or pending when accepted but unconfirmed. sent means dispatched for signing, not that all participants have signed; use the status tool for completed. Do not send again after sending_success or completed, or while a previous send is pending. Keep returned documentId, fileId, operationId, and trackingId when present. pending means accepted but completion is unconfirmed: check get_signature_document_status with documentId instead of resubmitting. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, a timeout, or a lost response may follow a successful submission; do not automatically repeat a preparation or send call. Inspect status when an ID is available; an empty status list does not make a retry safe. INVALID_REQUEST means inputs need correction; REQUEST_FAILED gives a referenceId for diagnosis. If the cause is unclear, ask for clarification or use the referenceId rather than guessing. Repeating a preparation can create another document. Use only the declared fields. Ask for missing facts instead of inventing values. Service credentials are configured on the server and must not be included in tool arguments.

coordinateSystem.description: Required: page_percent. All positions and sizes use 0-100 percentages of the visible PDF page, from its top-left. This explicit marker prevents old pixel/backend coordinates from being misinterpreted. Do not relabel old values; calculate their page percentages first.

documentId.description: Exact documentId returned by preparation for the existing document to send. Confirm preparation succeeded before calling. Do not invent an ID or substitute a fileId, operationId, or trackingId.

fileId.description: Exact fileId for the PDF in that prepared document, returned by preparation. Every supplied coordinate applies to this one file. Do not use a documentId, local path, or URL.

signatureCoordinates.description: Required nonempty signature-placement list for this PDF. In the combined tool, every signer needs at least one entry and every entry must refer to a supplied participant. For send-only, use the prepared document's participants and placements.

items.description: A signature placement for a document participant. Set coordinateSystem to page_percent. ALL field types use the same page-relative percentages: (0,0) is the top-left of the visible page, x increases rightward, y increases downward; 100 is the full page width or height, not 1. pageNumber is zero-based (0 is the first page). x/width are percentages of page width; y/height are percentages of page height. Positions must be >= 0, sizes > 0, x + width <= 100 and y + height <= 100. Example: x=10,y=80,width=30,height=10 starts 10% from the left and 80% from the top, covering 30% of page width and 10% of its height. The server reads each PDF page and handles backend units and field-specific conversions. Do not supply pixels, PDF points, or backend coordinates, or guess a placement from an unrelated image. Use the actual visible page and the user's intended field location. Unrepresentable placements, unreadable PDFs, 180-degree rotated placement pages, and text fields on rotated/cropped pages are rejected before sending; provide a flattened PDF if requested by the error. Provide at least one signatureCoordinates entry; optional coordinate arrays default to empty. Every coordinate's signatoryEmail must identify a participant in this document.

height.description: Field height as a percentage of visible page height; > 0, and y + height <= 100. Same units for every field type.

pageNumber.description: Zero-based PDF page number: 0 is the first page, 1 the second. Use an existing page in the actual PDF.

signatoryEmail.description: Valid email of the participant assigned to this field, without surrounding whitespace. Must match a participant in this document; normalized to lowercase. Use an email, not a signatory ID.

signatureImageFileId.description: Optional existing signature-image storage ID; nonempty when supplied. Never supply image bytes or a URL here. Omit unless required by a verified workflow; this field does not itself sign the document.

type.description: Optional SELISE field-type identifier; nonempty when supplied. Preserve a known value for this coordinate kind, or omit it. This is not a MIME type; no type catalog is provided by this tool.

width.description: Field width as a percentage of visible page width; > 0, and x + width <= 100. Same units for every field type.

x.description: Left edge as a percentage of visible page width, measured rightward from the top-left. 10 means 10%, not pixels or points. x + width must be <= 100.

y.description: Top edge as a percentage of visible page height, measured downward from the top-left. 80 means 80%. y + height must be <= 100.

simpleImageCoordinates.description: Optional simple-image placements for this PDF; defaults to []. Each entry requires a verified type and participant/page/position/size fields.

items.description: Optional simple-image placement in page percentages assigned to a participant. Requires type and all base coordinate fields; does not upload an image.

signatoryEmail.description: Valid email of the participant assigned to this field, without surrounding whitespace. Must match a participant in this document; normalized to lowercase. Use an email, not a signatory ID.

name: send_prepared_signature_document

anyOf.description: Result of sending an existing prepared document. sent is not completed signing.

documentId.description: Document identifier. Reuse as documentId in subsequent calls; an ID in an error response may be provisional and does not prove the document was created or the command accepted.

fileId.description: Storage identifier of the PDF. Reuse with its matching documentId when sending; not a download URL.

message.description: Optional human-readable progress or follow-up guidance. For pending results, check status rather than submitting again.

operationId.description: Identifier for tracing this tool operation. Not a document ID or proof of completion.

status.description: sent: sending confirmed, not completion of signing. pending: sending accepted but completion unconfirmed; use get_signature_document_status without resubmitting.

trackingId.description: Backend command correlation identifier, when available. Not a document ID or proof of completion.

anyOf.description: Error payload returned with the MCP result's isError flag set to true. Known IDs are optional and may be provisional; do not assume an error makes resubmission safe.

code.description: INVALID_REQUEST: input validation failed. REQUEST_FAILED: operation failed; use referenceId for diagnosis. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME: an action may have succeeded despite the error; inspect document status before considering a retry.

documentId.description: Document identifier. Reuse as documentId in subsequent calls; an ID in an error response may be provisional and does not prove the document was created or the command accepted.

fileId.description: Storage identifier of the PDF. Reuse with its matching documentId when sending; not a download URL.

message.description: Safe error explanation or recovery guidance; no private upstream diagnostics.

operationId.description: Identifier for tracing this tool operation. Not a document ID or proof of completion.

referenceId.description: Sentry error reference for support and diagnostics. Not a documentId or trackingId.

trackingId.description: Backend command correlation identifier, when available. Not a document ID or proof of completion.

outputSchema.description: Structured result: either the tool's success/progress payload or an error payload with code, message, and referenceId. Errors also set isError on the enclosing MCP result.
